bull_bear.body: Debt-funded growth within discipline: net debt Rs 3,864 cr (net debt/EBITDA 1.69x, net debt/equity 0.53x), rising with Rs 3,500 cr FY27 capex. Core business is the priority — paint investment capped at Rs 600 cr, to be grown on its own earnings; RMC capital-light (project enabler). Coal blocks reduce fuel risk + cost. 50 MT (FY30) long-term goal.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) **Fuel/energy shock** — pet-coke/diesel spike (geopolitical); Q2 cost +Rs 150/ton, peaking. 2) **Capacity constraint North/South** (~85-90%) caps growth to Central India only. 3) **EBITDA/ton compression** (Rs 982) until fuel normalizes + incentives restore. 4) **Monsoon deleverage** Q2. 5) **UAE white-cement disruption** (only GCC shipping) — console white growth "may not" be double-digit. 6) **Incentive trough** (GST-cut) until FY29 (~Rs 300 cr restored). 7) **Execution** — Jaisalmer/coal-block slippage; net-debt build. 8) **Imports resuming** (UAE clinker/cement trickling back) could re-pressure white/putty.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Ajay Saraogi confident on volume execution and cost-arbitrage, candid on near-term margin pressure and the Q2 cost step-up — precise on cost bridges (Rs 150/ton = Rs 100 fuel + Rs 50 diesel, ~1.75 Rs/Kcal peak), maintenance pre-ponement (~Rs 50 cr), fuel mix (40/45/balance), and incentive trajectory. Declined regional profitability/utilization disclosure. Held all expansion timelines despite peers pulling back ("no plans to reschedule… on schedule"). Transparent on one-offs and UAE volume loss. Tone: execution-focused, disciplined-growth, cautious on immediate pricing/margins.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The +19% grey volume is nearly all Central India** — North/South are capacity-locked (~85-90%), so JK's headline growth is a single-region cost-arbitrage story (domestic coal/AFR), not broad-based; sustaining double-digit needs Jaisalmer (H1FY28) and Central ramp.
- **Q1 print is flattered-and-punished at once** — flattered by UAE-import-disruption white/putty volume and share gains; punished by fuel shock + GST-compressed incentives (~Rs 50 cr) + pre-poned maintenance (~Rs 50 cr) → the Rs 982 EBITDA/ton understates normalized earning power, but Q2 gets worse (+Rs 150/ton) before relief.
- **Paint quietly hit EBITDA break-even in year 3** (Rs 125 cr Q1, capped at Rs 600 cr invest) and is helping putty volumes — a small but improving optionality, targeting 5-7% margin FY28.
- **RMC 5 → 17 → 50 → 100 plants is a channel play, not a margin play** (4-7% EBITDA) — it exists to defend/enter projects and pull cement + building-materials, first time broken out (Rs 35-40 cr Q1, ~Rs 250 cr FY27).
- **Incentive normalization to ~Rs 300 cr/yr is a FY29 earnings step-up** — GST-cut compressed it to ~Rs 50 cr/qtr now; new-unit eligibility (Buxar/Panna) restores it.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deck describes a 'steady debt profile': gross debt of Rs. 5,551 crore as on 30th June 2026 versus Rs. 5,136 crore as on 31st March 2026 (8% higher), with cash of Rs. 1,686 crore versus Rs. 1,765 crore (4% lower).
- Net debt of Rs. 3,864 crore as on 30th June 2026 versus Rs. 3,370 crore as on 31st March 2026 (15% higher), against equity of Rs. 7,252 crore versus Rs. 6,961 crore (4% higher).
- Leverage ratios as stated by the deck as on 30th June 2026: Net Debt/EBITDA of 1.69x and Net Debt/Equity of 0.53x.
- Rising net debt is being deployed into the Rs. 5,000-6,000 crore two-year capacity capex programme rather than any payout initiative; the deck contains no dividend or buyback commentary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Grey cement:** +19% YoY, all growth from Central India (new Bihar grinding); share gained in Central, held in North/South; North & South ~85-90% utilization (out of capacity). Panna overall utilization >65%.
- **White cement + putty:** white +11% YoY (+~28-29% by another cut, +~4% QoQ realization) — UAE-import disruption gave extra volume; competitiveness in putty/white will normalize. Nathdwara +0.6 MTPA putty (Q2) to cut toll dependence.
- **Paints (JK Maxx):** Q1 revenue Rs 125 cr, EBITDA break-even (up from ~Rs 100 cr/qtr prior 3 quarters, Rs 380 cr FY26); FY27 target Rs 500-550 cr; uses the JK Cement putty platform (service-charge model); Acro + Maxx brands. Helps putty volumes.
- **RMC:** 5 (exit-Mar) → 17 plants; Q1 revenue Rs 35-40 cr (vs ~Rs 5 cr Q4); exit ~Rs 100 cr/qtr; enables project entry (cement + building-materials pull). 4-7% EBITDA-margin business.
- **UAE (Fujairah):** lost ~50% of normal white-cement volume (only GCC region shipping available); dry-mix mortar local.

business.body:
- Among India's top five cement manufacturers, with 50+ years in grey cement and 40+ years in white cement.
- Scale metrics: 32.3 MTPA grey cement capacity (including 0.42 MTPA in subsidiary), 3.1 MTPA white cement and wall putty capacity (including 0.60 MTPA in subsidiary), and a distribution network of ~91,000 dealers and retailers.
- Portfolio spans grey cement, white cement, wall putty, tile adhesives and grouts, gypsum plaster, construction chemicals and paints.
- Deck frames sector demand as structurally upward: ~730 MTPA installed industry capacity with demand growth of 7-8% annually and healthy utilisation, with cement consumption split 57% housing, 30% infrastructure and 13% industrial and commercial.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [CSR] CSR spend of Rs. 11.7 crore in YTD June26, split Rs. 5.34 crore health (medical camps, mobile medical units, safe drinking water and a contribution to IIT-K for a 500 bed super speciality hospital), Rs. 5.09 crore education (school and university contributions) and Rs. 1.27 crore community development (vocational training for women, livestock improvement, rural entrepreneurship, community infrastructure, green initiatives and plantation drives).
- [Awards] Nimbahera integrated unit received the Golden Peacock Award 2026 at India's 27th International Conference on Environment Management & Climate Change; Jt. MD Madhavkrishna Singhania was honoured at the 2026 ASK Private Wealth Hurun India Forum & Awards.
- [Policy backdrop] Budget 2026-27 raises public infrastructure capital expenditure to Rs. 12.2 lakh crore, with infrastructure capex for FY27 estimated 17.7% higher than last fiscal; Rs. 3.10 lakh crore allocated for Road & Highways plus Rs. 1.22 lakh crore for road infrastructure and Rs. 1.87 lakh crore to NHAI; PMAY-G target of 20 million and PMAY-U target of 10 million additional houses for FY27; Indian GDP growth projected at 6.6% for FY27.
- [Cost pressure] Deck's own framing for the quarter: 'Robust volume growth, however reduced profitability due to cost pressure', with price increases and white-business growth from lower imports neutralising cost increases attributed to the geopolitical situation.

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 (from Rs 1,229 YoY / Rs 1,012 QoQ) on fuel/energy shock + GST-cut-compressed incentives (~Rs 50 cr) + ~Rs 50 cr pre-poned maintenance. Q2 cost +~Rs 150/ton (fuel +Rs 100 to ~1.75 Rs/Kcal peak + diesel/other +Rs 50), plus operating deleverage (monsoon seasonality); railways bulk-discount + lower packaging partly offset (North only). EBITDA Rs 639 cr (standalone; margin 16.9% vs 21.9% YoY), EBITDA/ton Rs 982 (vs Rs 1,229 YoY / Rs 1,012 QoQ), PAT Rs 291 cr (vs Rs 333 cr YoY), EPS Rs 35.90. Net debt Rs 3,864 cr (1.69x). outlook.body:
- **Grey volume 22.5-23 MT FY27** (double-digit growth; H2 "may not sustain" Q1's ~19% as base builds — implies ~6-7% for remaining quarters; management will "maximize" if demand holds).
- **Cost +~Rs 150/ton in Q2** (~Rs 100 fuel + ~Rs 50 diesel/other); **fuel cost peaks in Q2** (~1.75 Rs/Kcal from 1.53), decline thereafter; packaging flat/lower; Q2 maintenance similar/marginally lower.
- **Capacity: 40 MT by FY28, 50 MT by FY30** — "on schedule, no plans to reschedule." Jaisalmer greenfield (6 MT) commissioning **H1FY28**; Bhatinda grinding progressing; 2nd Punjab split-grinding land acquired.
- **Wall putty +0.6 MTPA (Nathdwara) commissioning Q2FY27** (reduce toll-manufacturing dependence; grow putty double-digit).
- **Panna Line 2 debottleneck 3.3 → 4 MT clinker this fiscal (FY27)**; no clinker shortage foreseen for Central India.
- **Paint (JK Maxx):** FY27 revenue Rs 500-550 cr (EBITDA break-even Q1 achieved, 3rd year of ops); FY28 EBITDA margin 5-7% with topline +~Rs 150 cr; investment capped at Rs 600 cr (core-business priority).
- **RMC:** 17 plants now → **50 by FY27, 100 by FY28**; FY27 revenue ~Rs 250 cr (maybe 300); ~breakeven FY27 (single-digit loss); structural margin only 4-7%.
- **Capex Rs 3,500 cr FY27, ~Rs 1,200 cr FY28** (+ next-leg expansion additional).
- **Coal blocks:** Mahan (larger) commissioning **end-FY28**, second ~1 yr later — substantial fuel-cost saving + risk reduction.
- **Incentives:** ~Rs 225-250 cr FY29, back to **~Rs 300 cr/yr** once new units (Buxar/Panna) restore eligibility.
- **Green power 75% by FY30** (ramp ~4-5%/yr from next year); thermal-substitution 35% FY30 target being reworked for new fuel mix.

risks.note: The industry added ~65 MnTPA in FY 2025-26 to reach ~730 MnTPA installed capacity and roughly 75 MnTPA more is anticipated in FY 2026-27; despite continued demand growth the operating rate is likely to moderate from ~74% to around 72% in FY 2026-27, with nearly 250 MnTPA more expected between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31 to reach ~975 MnTPA. The eastern region, followed by the northern and western regions, is expected to take the largest share of additions - the same regions into which the Company is expanding.
risks.risk: Industry overcapacity compressing utilisation and pricing

risks.note: Crude oil prices are cited at over $110 per barrel against a March 26 exit of $85, and rising geopolitical turmoil in West Asia including the war between the US and Iran has raised concerns over energy security and price volatility. Given India's substantial dependence on imported crude, sustained disruptions to global energy supply chains could lead to higher input costs and elevated inflation - a direct cost exposure for a fuel- and freight-intensive cement producer.
risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost inflation driven by crude oil and geopolitical disruption

risks.note: Management notes that exchange rate volatility and depreciation of the Indian rupee could further push up inflation by increasing the cost of energy and other essential imported items. The Company also has AED- and TZS-denominated overseas operations whose results are translated for reporting.

El Nino in the Pacific is described as a significant threat to economic activity in FY 2026-27, with IMD-projected rainfall around 90% of the Long Period Average and a 60% probability of a below-normal season, raising concerns for agriculture, food inflation and the broader economy. Rural housing is the principal driver of the housing segment on which cement demand most depends.

A large part of the demand narrative rests on government budget allocations - rural development, PMAY-G and PMAY-U, Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, NHAI and Railways - which makes volumes sensitive to fiscal priorities and execution rather than purely private demand.
risks.risk: Demand concentration in housing and government-funded construction

risks.note: The February 2026 India-US trade agreement cut US tariffs on Indian goods from 50% to 18% and affected 55% of India's $87 billion of exports to the US, with India agreeing to move towards zero tariffs and halt Russian crude purchases; world trade volume growth is expected to fall from 4.6% in 2025 to 1.9% in 2026. Trade policy uncertainty feeds directly into the input-cost and currency channels the Company is exposed to.

risks.risk: Realisation pressure in the white/putty business and loss-making newer subsidiaries
